eval_1_axe_a11y_testing.summary: The improved accessibility.md testing section directly transferred to all with-skill runs. Zero without-skill runs adopted any of the 5 key patterns, confirming these are genuinely additive to the model's base knowledge.

eval_2_modal_focus_trap.summary: LiveAnnouncer usage is the clearest differentiator (100% vs 33%). cdkFocusInitial improved but was partially known without skill. inert and host object are now universally adopted even without skill (model learned since iteration-1).

httpResource_error_flow_note.with_skill: 3/3 runs reference resource errors not reaching ErrorHandler

eval_3_http_error_handling.summary: Marginal skill lift. The improved error-handling.md patterns (typed ApiError, functional interceptor, effect-based httpResource error bridging) were largely matched by baseline knowledge. The resource-error-flow note is the only consistent differentiator.

notes: Quantitative pass rates remain 100% both configs -- assertions test broad capabilities the model knows regardless of skill.
The QUALITATIVE improvement is dramatic for eval 1 (axe a11y testing): 5 key patterns went from 0% to 100% adoption with the improved skill.
Eval 2 (modal) shows moderate lift: LiveAnnouncer (100% vs 33%) and consistent cdkFocusInitial usage.
Eval 3 (HTTP errors) shows minimal lift: the model already knows HTTP error patterns well.
With-skill runs use ~1.75x more tokens on average due to reading skill references.
Variance is low within configs: stddev ~15-20% of mean for both time and tokens.
The accessibility.md improvements are the clear winner -- they teach patterns genuinely absent from model training data.
